# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified playable-area coordinates. Validates coordinates, cell type, and occupancy.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if row is in [1, rows-2] and col is in [1, cols-2]. If not, return false.
  2. Get cell at cells[row][col].
  3. If cell is not a FillableCell, return false.
  4. If cell already has a pipe (pipe != null), return false.
  5. Set cell.pipe = pipe.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: cells, rows, cols
Related Classes: FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input: row - int (1-based internal row), col - int (1-based internal column), pipe - Pipe to place
Output: boolean - true if placement succeeded, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If successful, the specified cell now contains the given pipe.

Map::hasLost
Summary: Returns true when no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition).
Algorithm: Return prevFilledTiles == 0
Related Features: prevFilledTiles
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if loss condition is met
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

Map::undo
Summary: Removes the pipe from a cell at the given coordinate, used during undo operations.
Algorithm:
  1. Get cell at cells[coord.row][coord.col].
  2. If cell is a FillableCell, set its pipe to null.
Related Features: cells
Related Classes: FillableCell, Coordinate
Input: coord - Coordinate of the cell to clear
Output: void
Pre-condition: coord is within the playable area.
Post-condition: The pipe at the specified cell is removed.

Map::fillTiles
Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other).
Algorithm: 
  1. Initialize BFS queue with source cell
  2. For each distance step from 1 to distance:
     a. For each cell at current BFS frontier:
        - For each connection direction of the cell's pipe:
          - Calculate neighbor coordinate using direction offset
          - If neighbor is a FillableCell with a pipe:
            - Check if connections match (neighbor's connection opposite to current direction)
            - If match and not yet visited, add to next frontier
  3. Mark all visited cells as filled
  4. Update prevFilledTiles with count of newly filled tiles
Related Features: cells, sourceCell, filledTiles, prevFilledTiles
Related Classes: Coordinate, Direction, FillableCell, Pipe, TerminationCell
Input: distance (int) - how far water should flow
Output: None
Pre-condition: distance >= 0
Post-condition: Pipes within distance are filled if connections match

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation.
```

public boolean placePipe(final int row, final char col)
{
    // 1. Convert column letter to internal index
    int colIndex = col - 'A' + 1;
    // 2. Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipeQueue.peek())
    if (map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipeQueue.peek())) {
        // 3a. cellStack.push(cell at cells[row][colIndex])
        FillableCell cell = (FillableCell) map.getCell()[row][colIndex];
        cellStack.push(cell);
        // 3b. pipeQueue.consume()
        pipeQueue.consume();
        // 3c. numOfSteps++
        numOfSteps++;
        // 3d. Return true
        return true;
    }
    // 4. Otherwise return false
    return false;
}

public void skipPipe()
{
    // 1. pipeQueue.consume()
    pipeQueue.consume();
    // 2. numOfSteps++
    numOfSteps++;
}

public boolean undoStep()
{
    // 1. cell = cellStack.pop()
    FillableCell cell = cellStack.pop();
    // 2. If cell is null, return false
    if (cell == null) {
        return false;
    }
    // 3. map.undo(cell.coord)
    map.undo(cell.getCoord());
    // 4. pipeQueue.undo(cell.pipe)
    pipeQueue.undo(cell.getPipe());
    // 5. numOfSteps++
    numOfSteps++;
    // 6. Return true
    return true;
}

    // 1. delayBar.countdown()
    delayBar.countdown();
    // 2. If delayBar.distance() > 0:
    if (delayBar.distance() > 0) {

    return map.checkPath();

1. Compute context information
  1.1 Navigate the Ecore model to find related classes
  1.2 Also consider the related classes in the Javadocs.
  1.3 Locate these files in your project.
  1.4 Generate the class summarization.
2. A method is unimplemented if its body contains `// TODO: Please complete this Java method based on the docstring`.

  3.1 You must read the docstring of this method. The fragment between `<!-- begin-model-doc -->` and `<!-- end-model-doc -->` contains the method specification;
  3.2 Generate your code strictly according to the algorithm; Be aware of the EMF code style and APIs;
  3.3 You should not change the method signature;
  3.4 After generation, replace the current body with the one you generate;
  3.5 Keep and update the docstring by changing `@generated` to `@generated NOT`.
4. Check the import list. Add missing imports if needed.
5. Do not change other part.
6. Be aware of the method signatures, particularly, the input and output types, provided in the **Context**.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

public void fillTiles(final int distance)
{
    if (distance < 0) return;
    
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[rows][cols];
    EList<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    // Get source cell's neighbor in pointingTo direction
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null || source.getPointingTo() == null) return;
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    Direction pointingTo = source.getPointingTo();
    
    // Calculate neighbor coordinate based on direction
    int dr = 0, dc = 0;
    switch (pointingTo.getValue()) {
        case Direction.UP_VALUE:
            dr = -1; dc = 0; break;
        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
            dr = 1; dc = 0; break;
        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
            dr = 0; dc = -1; break;
        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
            dr = 0; dc = 1; break;
    }
    
    int startRow = sourceCoord.getRow() + dr;
    int startCol = sourceCoord.getCol() + dc;
    
    if (startRow < 0 || startRow >= rows || startCol < 0 || startCol >= cols) {
        // No valid starting point
        setPrevFilledTiles(0);
        return;
    }
    
    Cell startCell = getCell()[startRow][startCol];
    if (startCell instanceof FillableCell && ((FillableCell)startCell).getPipe() != null) {
        Coordinate startCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
        startCoord.setRow(startRow);
        startCoord.setCol(startCol);
        currentFrontier.add(startCoord);
        visited[startRow][startCol] = true;
    }
    
    int newlyFilled = 0;
    boolean sinkReached = false;
    
    for (int step = 1; step <= distance && !currentFrontier.isEmpty(); step++) {
        EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
        
        for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
            int r = coord.getRow();
            int c = coord.getCol();
            Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
            
            if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) continue;
            FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
            Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
            if (pipe == null) continue;
            
            for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
                int nr = r, nc = c;
                switch (dir.getValue()) {
                    case Direction.UP_VALUE: nr = r - 1; break;
                    case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: nr = r + 1; break;
                    case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: nc = c - 1; break;
                    case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: nc = c + 1; break;
                }
                
                if (nr < 0 || nr >= rows || nc < 0 || nc >= cols) continue;
                if (visited[nr][nc]) continue;
                
                Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
                
                // Check if sink reached
                if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                    TerminationCell sink = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
                    if (sink == getSinkCell()) {
                        // Check if connections match
                        Direction opposite = getOpposite(dir);
                        if (sink.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
                            sinkReached = true;
                        }
                    }
                }
                
                if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                    FillableCell neighborFc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
                    Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFc.getPipe();
                    if (neighborPipe != null) {
                        Direction opposite = getOpposite(dir);
                        if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                            Coordinate nextCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                            nextCoord.setRow(nr);
                            nextCoord.setCol(nc);
                            nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                            visited[nr][nc] = true;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        
        // Mark cells in current frontier as filled
        for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
            Cell cell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
            if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
                if (fc.getPipe() != null && !fc.getPipe().isFilled()) {
                    fc.getPipe().setFilled(true);
                    newlyFilled++;
                }
            }
        }
        
        if (sinkReached) {
            // Mark sink as filled
            if (getSinkCell() != null) {
                getSinkCell().setFilled(true);
            }
            break;
        }
        
        currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
    }
    
    // If loop ended without breaking (sink not reached), still mark the last frontier
    if (!sinkReached) {
        for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
            Cell cell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
            if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
                if (fc.getPipe() != null && !fc.getPipe().isFilled()) {
                    fc.getPipe().setFilled(true);
                    newlyFilled++;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
}

  /**

   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion. The source termination cell is already filled before this method is called.
   * Algorithm:

   * Output: None

   * Post-condition: Pipes within distance from source are filled if connections match; prevFilledTiles is updated with the count of newly filled tiles
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->

  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {

      setPrevFilledTiles(0);

    EList<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();

      case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
        dr = 1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = -1; break;
      case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = 1; break;
    }

    int startCol = sourceCoord.getCol() + dc;

        startCoord.setRow(startRow);
        startCoord.setCol(startCol);

        int r = coord.getRow();

            case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: nr = r + 1; break;
            case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: nc = c - 1; break;
            case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: nc = c + 1; break;

    // Actually, the loop already processes each step's frontier. If the loop ends because step > distance,
    // the last frontier has already been processed. So we're good.
    
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);

  private Direction getOppositeDirection(Direction dir) {
    switch (dir.getValue()) {

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
```java
   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). The source termination cell is already filled before this method is called.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize BFS queue with the source cell's neighbor in the pointingTo direction
   *   2. For each distance step from 1 to distance:
   *      a. For each cell at current BFS frontier:
   *         - For each connection direction of the cell's pipe:
   *           - Calculate neighbor coordinate using direction offset
   *           - If neighbor is a FillableCell with a pipe:
   *             - Check if connections match (neighbor's connection opposite to current direction)
   *             - If match and not yet visited, add to next frontier
   *      b. If the SINK termination cell is reached, stop early
   *   3. Mark all visited cells as filled
   *   4. Update prevFilledTiles with count of newly filled tiles
   * Related Features: cells, sourceCell, filledTiles, prevFilledTiles
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Direction, FillableCell, Pipe, TerminationCell
   * Input: distance (int) - how far water should flow
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: distance >= 0; sourceCell is already filled
   * Post-condition: Pipes within distance from source are filled if connections match; prevFilledTiles is updated with the count of newly filled tiles
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    if (distance < 0) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[getRows()][getCols()];
    EList<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null || source.getPointingTo() == null) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    Direction pointingTo = source.getPointingTo();
    
    // Calculate neighbor coordinate based on pointingTo direction
    int dr = 0, dc = 0;
    switch (pointingTo.getValue()) {
      case Direction.UP_VALUE:
        dr = -1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
        dr = 1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = -1; break;
      case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = 1; break;
    }
    
    int startRow = sourceCoord.getRow() + dr;
    int startCol = sourceCoord.getCol() + dc;
    
    if (startRow >= 0 && startRow < getRows() && startCol >= 0 && startCol < getCols()) {
      Cell startCell = getCell()[startRow][startCol];
      if (startCell instanceof FillableCell && ((FillableCell) startCell).getPipe() != null) {
        Coordinate startCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
        startCoord.setRow(startRow);
        startCoord.setCol(startCol);
        currentFrontier.add(startCoord);
        visited[startRow][startCol] = true;
      }
    }
    
    int newlyFilled = 0;
    boolean sinkReached = false;
    
    for (int step = 1; step <= distance && !currentFrontier.isEmpty() && !sinkReached; step++) {
      EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        int r = coord.getRow();
        int c = coord.getCol();
        Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
        
        if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) continue;
        FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
        Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
        if (pipe == null) continue;
        
        for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
          int nr = r, nc = c;
          switch (dir.getValue()) {
            case Direction.UP_VALUE: nr = r - 1; break;
            case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: nr = r + 1; break;
            case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: nc = c - 1; break;
            case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: nc = c + 1; break;
          }
          
          if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
          if (visited[nr][nc]) continue;
          
          Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
          
          // Check if sink termination cell is reached
          if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell && neighborCell == getSinkCell()) {
            TerminationCell sink = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
            Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
            if (sink.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
              sinkReached = true;
            }
            continue;
          }
          
          if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell neighborFc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFc.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe != null) {
              Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
              if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                Coordinate nextCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                nextCoord.setRow(nr);
                nextCoord.setCol(nc);
                nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                visited[nr][nc] = true;
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      // Mark cells in current frontier as filled
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
          Pipe p = fc.getPipe();
          if (p != null && !p.isFilled()) {
            p.setFilled(true);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      
      if (sinkReached) {
        getSinkCell().setFilled(true);
        break;
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
    }
    
    // If sink was not reached and there are remaining cells in the frontier (from the last step that didn't execute)
    // Actually, the loop already processes each step's frontier. If the loop ends because step > distance,
    // the last frontier has already been processed. So we're good.
    
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
  }
```

```
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
```
```java
      return;
    }
    
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[getRows()][getCols()];
    EList<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null || source.getPointingTo() == null) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    Direction pointingTo = source.getPointingTo();
    
    // Calculate neighbor coordinate based on pointingTo direction
    int dr = 0, dc = 0;
    switch (pointingTo.getValue()) {
      case Direction.UP_VALUE:
        dr = -1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
        dr = 1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = -1; break;
      case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = 1; break;
    }
    
    int startRow = sourceCoord.getRow() + dr;
    int startCol = sourceCoord.getCol() + dc;
    
    if (startRow >= 0 && startRow < getRows() && startCol >= 0 && startCol < getCols()) {
      Cell startCell = getCell()[startRow][startCol];
      if (startCell instanceof FillableCell && ((FillableCell) startCell).getPipe() != null) {
        Coordinate startCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
        startCoord.setRow(startRow);
        startCoord.setCol(startCol);
        currentFrontier.add(startCoord);
        visited[startRow][startCol] = true;
      }
    }
    
    int newlyFilled = 0;
    boolean sinkReached = false;
    
    for (int step = 1; step <= distance && !currentFrontier.isEmpty() && !sinkReached; step++) {
      EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        int r = coord.getRow();
        int c = coord.getCol();
        Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
        
        if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) continue;
        FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
        Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();

        for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
          int nr = r, nc = c;
          switch (dir.getValue()) {
            case Direction.UP_VALUE: nr = r - 1; break;
            case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: nr = r + 1; break;
            case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: nc = c - 1; break;
            case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: nc = c + 1; break;
          }
          
          if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
          if (visited[nr][nc]) continue;

          if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell && neighborCell == getSinkCell()) {
            TerminationCell sink = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
            Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
            if (sink.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
              sinkReached = true;
            }
            continue;
          }
          
          if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell neighborFc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFc.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe != null) {

                nextCoord.setCol(nc);
                nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
```

```java
   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). The source termination cell is already filled before this method is called.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize BFS queue with the source cell's neighbor in the pointingTo direction
   *   2. For each distance step from 1 to distance:
   *      a. For each cell at current BFS frontier:
   *         - For each connection direction of the cell's pipe:
   *           - Calculate neighbor coordinate using direction offset
   *           - If neighbor is a FillableCell with a pipe:
   *             - Check if connections match (neighbor's connection opposite to current direction)
   *             - If match and not yet visited, add to next frontier
   *      b. If the SINK termination cell is reached, stop early
   *   3. Mark all visited cells as filled
   *   4. Update prevFilledTiles with count of newly filled tiles
   * Related Features: cells, sourceCell, filledTiles, prevFilledTiles
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Direction, FillableCell, Pipe, TerminationCell
   * Input: distance (int) - how far water should flow
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: distance >= 0; sourceCell is already filled
   * Post-condition: Pipes within distance from source are filled if connections match; prevFilledTiles is updated with the count of newly filled tiles
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    if (distance < 0) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[getRows()][getCols()];
    EList<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null || source.getPointingTo() == null) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    Direction pointingTo = source.getPointingTo();
    
    // Calculate neighbor coordinate based on pointingTo direction
    int dr = 0, dc = 0;
    switch (pointingTo.getValue()) {
      case Direction.UP_VALUE:
        dr = -1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
        dr = 1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = -1; break;
      case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = 1; break;
    }
    
    int startRow = sourceCoord.getRow() + dr;
    int startCol = sourceCoord.getCol() + dc;
    
    if (startRow >= 0 && startRow < getRows() && startCol >= 0 && startCol < getCols()) {
      Cell startCell = getCell()[startRow][startCol];
      if (startCell instanceof FillableCell && ((FillableCell) startCell).getPipe() != null) {
        Coordinate startCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
        startCoord.setRow(startRow);
        startCoord.setCol(startCol);
        currentFrontier.add(startCoord);
        visited[startRow][startCol] = true;
      }
    }
    
    int newlyFilled = 0;
    boolean sinkReached = false;
    
    for (int step = 1; step <= distance && !currentFrontier.isEmpty() && !sinkReached; step++) {
      EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        int r = coord.getRow();
        int c = coord.getCol();
        Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
        
        if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) continue;
        FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
        Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
        if (pipe == null) continue;
        
        for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
          int nr = r, nc = c;
          switch (dir.getValue()) {
            case Direction.UP_VALUE: nr = r - 1; break;
            case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: nr = r + 1; break;
            case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: nc = c - 1; break;
            case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: nc = c + 1; break;
          }
          
          if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
          if (visited[nr][nc]) continue;
          
          Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
          
          // Check if sink termination cell is reached
          if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell && neighborCell == getSinkCell()) {
            TerminationCell sink = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
            Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
            if (sink.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
              sinkReached = true;
            }
            continue;
          }
          
          if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell neighborFc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFc.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe != null) {
              Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
              if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                Coordinate nextCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                nextCoord.setRow(nr);
                nextCoord.setCol(nc);
                nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                visited[nr][nc] = true;
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      // Mark cells in current frontier as filled
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
          Pipe p = fc.getPipe();
          if (p != null && !p.isFilled()) {
            p.setFilled(true);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      
      if (sinkReached) {
        getSinkCell().setFilled(true);
        break;
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
    }
    
    // If sink was not reached and there are remaining cells in the frontier (from the last step that didn't execute)
    // Actually, the loop already processes each step's frontier. If the loop ends because step > distance,
    // the last frontier has already been processed. So we're good.
    
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
  }
```

```java
   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). The source termination cell is already filled before this method is called.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize BFS queue with the source cell's neighbor in the pointingTo direction
   *   2. For each distance step from 1 to distance:
   *      a. For each cell at current BFS frontier:
   *         - For each connection direction of the cell's pipe:
   *           - Calculate neighbor coordinate using direction offset
   *           - If neighbor is a FillableCell with a pipe:
   *             - Check if connections match (neighbor's connection opposite to current direction)
   *             - If match and not yet visited, add to next frontier
   *      b. If the SINK termination cell is reached, stop early
   *   3. Mark all visited cells as filled
   *   4. Update prevFilledTiles with count of newly filled tiles
   * Related Features: cells, sourceCell, filledTiles, prevFilledTiles
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Direction, FillableCell, Pipe, TerminationCell
   * Input: distance (int) - how far water should flow
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: distance >= 0; sourceCell is already filled
   * Post-condition: Pipes within distance from source are filled if connections match; prevFilledTiles is updated with the count of newly filled tiles
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    if (distance < 0) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[getRows()][getCols()];
    EList<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null || source.getPointingTo() == null) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    Direction pointingTo = source.getPointingTo();
    
    // Calculate neighbor coordinate based on pointingTo direction
    int dr = 0, dc = 0;
    switch (pointingTo.getValue()) {
      case Direction.UP_VALUE:
        dr = -1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
        dr = 1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = -1; break;
      case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = 1; break;
    }
    
    int startRow = sourceCoord.getRow() + dr;
    int startCol = sourceCoord.getCol() + dc;
    
    if (startRow >= 0 && startRow < getRows() && startCol >= 0 && startCol < getCols()) {
      Cell startCell = getCell()[startRow][startCol];
      if (startCell instanceof FillableCell && ((FillableCell) startCell).getPipe() != null) {
        Coordinate startCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
        startCoord.setRow(startRow);
        startCoord.setCol(startCol);
        currentFrontier.add(startCoord);
        visited[startRow][startCol] = true;
      }
    }
    
    int newlyFilled = 0;
    boolean sinkReached = false;
    
    for (int step = 1; step <= distance && !currentFrontier.isEmpty() && !sinkReached; step++) {
      EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        int r = coord.getRow();
        int c = coord.getCol();
        Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
        
        if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) continue;
        FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
        Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
        if (pipe == null) continue;
        
        for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
          int nr = r, nc = c;
          switch (dir.getValue()) {
            case Direction.UP_VALUE: nr = r - 1; break;
            case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: nr = r + 1; break;
            case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: nc = c - 1; break;
            case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: nc = c + 1; break;
          }
          
          if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
          if (visited[nr][nc]) continue;
          
          Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
          
          // Check if sink termination cell is reached
          if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell && neighborCell == getSinkCell()) {
            TerminationCell sink = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
            Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
            if (sink.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
              sinkReached = true;
            }
            continue;
          }
          
          if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell neighborFc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFc.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe != null) {
              Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
              if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                Coordinate nextCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                nextCoord.setRow(nr);
                nextCoord.setCol(nc);
                nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                visited[nr][nc] = true;
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      // Mark cells in current frontier as filled
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
          Pipe p = fc.getPipe();
          if (p != null && !p.isFilled()) {
            p.setFilled(true);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      
      if (sinkReached) {
        getSinkCell().setFilled(true);
        break;
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
    }
    
    // If sink was not reached and there are remaining cells in the frontier (from the last step that didn't execute)
    // Actually, the loop already processes each step's frontier. If the loop ends because step > distance,
    // the last frontier has already been processed. So we're good.
    
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
  }
```

```java
   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). The source termination cell is already filled before this method is called.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize BFS queue with the source cell's neighbor in the pointingTo direction
   *   2. For each distance step from 1 to distance:
   *      a. For each cell at current BFS frontier:
   *         - For each connection direction of the cell's pipe:
   *           - Calculate neighbor coordinate using direction offset
   *           - If neighbor is a FillableCell with a pipe:
   *             - Check if connections match (neighbor's connection opposite to current direction)
   *             - If match and not yet visited, add to next frontier
   *      b. If the SINK termination cell is reached, stop early
   *   3. Mark all visited cells as filled
   *   4. Update prevFilledTiles with count of newly filled tiles
   * Related Features: cells, sourceCell, filledTiles, prevFilledTiles
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Direction, FillableCell, Pipe, TerminationCell
   * Input: distance (int) - how far water should flow
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: distance >= 0; sourceCell is already filled
   * Post-condition: Pipes within distance from source are filled if connections match; prevFilledTiles is updated with the count of newly filled tiles
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    if (distance < 0) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[getRows()][getCols()];
    EList<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null || source.getPointingTo() == null) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    Direction pointingTo = source.getPointingTo();
    
    // Calculate neighbor coordinate based on pointingTo direction
    int dr = 0, dc = 0;
    switch (pointingTo.getValue()) {
      case Direction.UP_VALUE:
        dr = -1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
        dr = 1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = -1; break;
      case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = 1; break;
    }
    
    int startRow = sourceCoord.getRow() + dr;
    int startCol = sourceCoord.getCol() + dc;
    
    if (startRow >= 0 && startRow < getRows() && startCol >= 0 && startCol < getCols()) {
      Cell startCell = getCell()[startRow][startCol];
      if (startCell instanceof FillableCell && ((FillableCell) startCell).getPipe() != null) {
        Coordinate startCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
        startCoord.setRow(startRow);
        startCoord.setCol(startCol);
        currentFrontier.add(startCoord);
        visited[startRow][startCol] = true;
      }
    }
    
    int newlyFilled = 0;
    boolean sinkReached = false;
    
    for (int step = 1; step <= distance && !currentFrontier.isEmpty() && !sinkReached; step++) {
      EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        int r = coord.getRow();
        int c = coord.getCol();
        Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
        
        if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) continue;
        FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
        Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
        if (pipe == null) continue;
        
        for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
          int nr = r, nc = c;
          switch (dir.getValue()) {
            case Direction.UP_VALUE: nr = r - 1; break;
            case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: nr = r + 1; break;
            case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: nc = c - 1; break;
            case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: nc = c + 1; break;
          }
          
          if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
          if (visited[nr][nc]) continue;
          
          Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
          
          // Check if sink termination cell is reached
          if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell && neighborCell == getSinkCell()) {
            TerminationCell sink = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
            Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
            if (sink.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
              sinkReached = true;
            }
            continue;
          }
          
          if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell neighborFc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFc.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe != null) {
              Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
              if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                Coordinate nextCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                nextCoord.setRow(nr);
                nextCoord.setCol(nc);
                nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                visited[nr][nc] = true;
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      // Mark cells in current frontier as filled
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
          Pipe p = fc.getPipe();
          if (p != null && !p.isFilled()) {
            p.setFilled(true);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      
      if (sinkReached) {
        getSinkCell().setFilled(true);
        break;
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
    }
    
    // If sink was not reached and there are remaining cells in the frontier (from the last step that didn't execute)
    // Actually, the loop already processes each step's frontier. If the loop ends because step > distance,
    // the last frontier has already been processed. So we're good.
    
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
  }
```

```java
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). The source termination cell is already filled before this method is called.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize BFS queue with the source cell's neighbor in the pointingTo direction
   *   2. For each distance step from 1 to distance:
   *      a. For each cell at current BFS frontier:
   *         - For each connection direction of the cell's pipe:
   *           - Calculate neighbor coordinate using direction offset
   *           - If neighbor is a FillableCell with a pipe:
   *             - Check if connections match (neighbor's connection opposite to current direction)
   *             - If match and not yet visited, add to next frontier
   *      b. If the SINK termination cell is reached, stop early
   *   3. Mark all visited cells as filled
   *   4. Update prevFilledTiles with count of newly filled tiles
   * Related Features: cells, sourceCell, filledTiles, prevFilledTiles
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Direction, FillableCell, Pipe, TerminationCell
   * Input: distance (int) - how far water should flow
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: distance >= 0; sourceCell is already filled
   * Post-condition: Pipes within distance from source are filled if connections match; prevFilledTiles is updated with the count of newly filled tiles
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    if (distance < 0) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[getRows()][getCols()];
    EList<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null || source.getPointingTo() == null) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    Direction pointingTo = source.getPointingTo();
    
    // Calculate neighbor coordinate based on pointingTo direction
    int dr = 0, dc = 0;
    switch (pointingTo.getValue()) {
      case Direction.UP_VALUE:
        dr = -1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
        dr = 1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = -1; break;
      case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = 1; break;
    }
    
    int startRow = sourceCoord.getRow() + dr;
    int startCol = sourceCoord.getCol() + dc;
    
    if (startRow >= 0 && startRow < getRows() && startCol >= 0 && startCol < getCols()) {
      Cell startCell = getCell()[startRow][startCol];
      if (startCell instanceof FillableCell && ((FillableCell) startCell).getPipe() != null) {
        Coordinate startCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
        startCoord.setRow(startRow);
        startCoord.setCol(startCol);
        currentFrontier.add(startCoord);
        visited[startRow][startCol] = true;
      }
    }
    
    int newlyFilled = 0;
    boolean sinkReached = false;
    
    for (int step = 1; step <= distance && !currentFrontier.isEmpty() && !sinkReached; step++) {
      EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        int r = coord.getRow();
        int c = coord.getCol();
        Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
        
        if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) continue;
        FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
        Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
        if (pipe == null) continue;
        
        for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
          int nr = r, nc = c;
          switch (dir.getValue()) {
            case Direction.UP_VALUE: nr = r - 1; break;
            case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: nr = r + 1; break;
            case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: nc = c - 1; break;
            case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: nc = c + 1; break;
          }
          
          if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
          if (visited[nr][nc]) continue;
          
          Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
          
          // Check if sink termination cell is reached
          if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell && neighborCell == getSinkCell()) {
            TerminationCell sink = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
            Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
            if (sink.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
              sinkReached = true;
            }
            continue;
          }
          
          if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell neighborFc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFc.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe != null) {
              Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
              if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                Coordinate nextCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                nextCoord.setRow(nr);
                nextCoord.setCol(nc);
                nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                visited[nr][nc] = true;
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      // Mark cells in current frontier as filled
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
          Pipe p = fc.getPipe();
          if (p != null && !p.isFilled()) {
            p.setFilled(true);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      
      if (sinkReached) {
        getSinkCell().setFilled(true);
        break;
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
    }
    
    // If sink was not reached and there are remaining cells in the frontier (from the last step that didn't execute)
    // Actually, the loop already processes each step's frontier. If the loop ends because step > distance,
    // the last frontier has already been processed. So we're good.
    
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
  }
```

```java
   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). The source termination cell is already filled before this method is called.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize BFS queue with the source cell's neighbor in the pointingTo direction
   *   2. For each distance step from 1 to distance:
   *      a. For each cell at current BFS frontier:
   *         - For each connection direction of the cell's pipe:
   *           - Calculate neighbor coordinate using direction offset
   *           - If neighbor is a FillableCell with a pipe:
   *             - Check if connections match (neighbor's connection opposite to current direction)
   *             - If match and not yet visited, add to next frontier
   *      b. If the SINK termination cell is reached, stop early
   *   3. Mark all visited cells as filled
   *   4. Update prevFilledTiles with count of newly filled tiles
   * Related Features: cells, sourceCell, filledTiles, prevFilledTiles
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Direction, FillableCell, Pipe, TerminationCell
   * Input: distance (int) - how far water should flow
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: distance >= 0; sourceCell is already filled
   * Post-condition: Pipes within distance from source are filled if connections match; prevFilledTiles is updated with the count of newly filled tiles
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    if (distance < 0) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[getRows()][getCols()];
    EList<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null || source.getPointingTo() == null) {
      setPrevFilledTiles(0);
      return;
    }
    
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    Direction pointingTo = source.getPointingTo();
    
    // Calculate neighbor coordinate based on pointingTo direction
    int dr = 0, dc = 0;
    switch (pointingTo.getValue()) {
      case Direction.UP_VALUE:
        dr = -1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
        dr = 1; dc = 0; break;
      case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = -1; break;
      case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
        dr = 0; dc = 1; break;
    }
    
    int startRow = sourceCoord.getRow() + dr;
    int startCol = sourceCoord.getCol() + dc;
    
    if (startRow >= 0 && startRow < getRows() && startCol >= 0 && startCol < getCols()) {
      Cell startCell = getCell()[startRow][startCol];
      if (startCell instanceof FillableCell && ((FillableCell) startCell).getPipe() != null) {
        Coordinate startCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
        startCoord.setRow(startRow);
        startCoord.setCol(startCol);
        currentFrontier.add(startCoord);
        visited[startRow][startCol] = true;
      }
    }
    
    int newlyFilled = 0;
    boolean sinkReached = false;
    
    for (int step = 1; step <= distance && !currentFrontier.isEmpty() && !sinkReached; step++) {
      EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        int r = coord.getRow();
        int c = coord.getCol();
        Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
        
        if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) continue;
        FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
        Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
        if (pipe == null) continue;
        
        for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
          int nr = r, nc = c;
          switch (dir.getValue()) {
            case Direction.UP_VALUE: nr = r - 1; break;
            case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: nr = r + 1; break;
            case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: nc = c - 1; break;
            case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: nc = c + 1; break;
          }
          
          if (nr < 0 || nr >= getRows() || nc < 0 || nc >= getCols()) continue;
          if (visited[nr][nc]) continue;
          
          Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
          
          // Check if sink termination cell is reached
          if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell && neighborCell == getSinkCell()) {
            TerminationCell sink = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
            Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
            if (sink.getPointingTo() == opposite) {
              sinkReached = true;
            }
            continue;
          }
          
          if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
            FillableCell neighborFc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFc.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe != null) {
              Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(dir);
              if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                Coordinate nextCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
                nextCoord.setRow(nr);
                nextCoord.setCol(nc);
                nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                visited[nr][nc] = true;
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      // Mark cells in current frontier as filled
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = getCell()[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
          Pipe p = fc.getPipe();
          if (p != null && !p.isFilled()) {
            p.setFilled(true);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      
      if (sinkReached) {
        getSinkCell().setFilled(true);
        break;
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
    }
    
    // If sink was not reached and there are remaining cells in the frontier (from the last step that didn't execute)
    // Actually, the loop already processes each step's frontier. If the loop ends because step > distance,
    // the last frontier has already been processed. So we're good.
    
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
  }
```

```java
   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). The source termination cell is already filled before this method is called.

   * Post-condition: Pipes within distance from source are filled if connections match; prevFilledTiles is updated with the count of newly filled tiles
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->

   * @generated NOT
```
