# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Pipe::getConnections
Summary: Returns the list of connection directions for this pipe based on its shape.
Algorithm: Switch on shape:
  - HORIZONTAL: return [LEFT, RIGHT]
  - VERTICAL: return [UP, DOWN]
  - TOP_LEFT: return [UP, LEFT]
  - TOP_RIGHT: return [UP, RIGHT]
  - BOTTOM_LEFT: return [DOWN, LEFT]
  - BOTTOM_RIGHT: return [DOWN, RIGHT]
  - CROSS: return [UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT]
  - default: throw IllegalStateException("Unknown shape")
Related Features: shape field.
Related Classes: Direction, PipeShape
Input: None
Output: List<Direction> - list of connection directions for this pipe.
Pre-condition: shape must be a valid PipeShape enum value.
Post-condition: Returns the appropriate list of directions for the pipe's shape.

# Operation Specifications
Pipe::getConnections
Summary: Returns the list of connection directions for this pipe based on its shape.
Algorithm: Switch on shape:
  - HORIZONTAL: return [LEFT, RIGHT]
  - VERTICAL: return [UP, DOWN]
  - TOP_LEFT: return [UP, LEFT]
  - TOP_RIGHT: return [UP, RIGHT]
  - BOTTOM_LEFT: return [DOWN, LEFT]
  - BOTTOM_RIGHT: return [DOWN, RIGHT]
  - CROSS: return [UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT]
  - default: throw IllegalStateException("Unknown shape")
Related Features: shape field.
Related Classes: Direction, PipeShape
Input: None
Output: List<Direction> - list of connection directions for this pipe.
Pre-condition: shape must be a valid PipeShape enum value.
Post-condition: Returns the appropriate list of directions for the pipe's shape.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Map::undo
Summary: Removes a pipe from the specified coordinate and clears the cell.
Algorithm:
  1. Get the cell at the given coordinate.
  2. If the cell is a FillableCell, set its pipe to null.
Related Features: cells field.
Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell
Input: coord : Coordinate - the coordinate of the cell to undo.
Output: void
Pre-condition: coord is within the playable area.
Post-condition: The pipe at the specified coordinate is removed (set to null).

Map::fillTiles
Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from the source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along connected pipes with matching directions.
Algorithm:
  1. If distance == 1, call fillBeginTile() first.
  2. Perform BFS starting from the source cell's adjacent cell in the source's pointingTo direction.
  3. For each step, explore neighbors in the pipe's connection directions.
  4. Only propagate to a neighbor if: (a) the neighbor is a FillableCell with a pipe, (b) the neighbor's pipe has a connection in the opposite direction of the current pipe's connection, and (c) the BFS depth is within the given distance.
  5. Mark reached cells as filled.
  6. Update filledTiles list and prevFilledTiles with the count of newly filled tiles in this round.
Related Features: filledTiles, prevFilledTiles, sourceCell, cells fields.
Related Classes: Coordinate, Direction, Cell, FillableCell, Pipe, TerminationCell
Input: distance : int - the maximum distance (number of steps) water should flow from the source (positive integer).
Output: void
Pre-condition: distance >= 0
Post-condition: Pipes within the specified distance that are connected to the source are marked as filled. filledTiles and prevFilledTiles are updated.

Map::hasLost
Summary: Checks the loss condition: returns true if no new pipes were filled in the previous round.
Algorithm: Return (prevFilledTiles == 0).
Related Features: prevFilledTiles field.
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no new tiles were filled in the previous round, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the loss status based on prevFilledTiles.

Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified internal coordinates. Validates coordinates, cell type, and occupancy.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if row is in [1, rows-2] and col is in [1, cols-2]. If not, return false.
  2. Get the cell at cells[row][col].
  3. If the cell is not a FillableCell, return false.
  4. If the cell already has a pipe (pipe field not null), return false.
  5. Set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true.
Related Features: cells, rows, cols fields.
Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe
Input: row : int - internal row index (1 to rows-2). col : int - internal column index (1 to cols-2). pipe : Pipe - the pipe to place.
Output: boolean - true if the pipe was successfully placed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: pipe is not null.
Post-condition: If successful, the specified cell's pipe is set to the given pipe. Otherwise, nothing changes.

# Operation Specifications
Map::undo
Summary: Removes a pipe from the specified coordinate and clears the cell.
Algorithm:
  1. Get the cell at the given coordinate.
  2. If the cell is a FillableCell, set its pipe to null.
Related Features: cells field.
Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell
Input: coord : Coordinate - the coordinate of the cell to undo.
Output: void
Pre-condition: coord is within the playable area.
Post-condition: The pipe at the specified coordinate is removed (set to null).

Map::fillTiles
Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from the source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along connected pipes with matching directions.
Algorithm:
  1. If distance == 1, call fillBeginTile() first.
  2. Perform BFS starting from the source cell's adjacent cell in the source's pointingTo direction.
  3. For each step, explore neighbors in the pipe's connection directions.
  4. Only propagate to a neighbor if: (a) the neighbor is a FillableCell with a pipe, (b) the neighbor's pipe has a connection in the opposite direction of the current pipe's connection, and (c) the BFS depth is within the given distance.
  5. Mark reached cells as filled.
  6. Update filledTiles list and prevFilledTiles with the count of newly filled tiles in this round.
Related Features: filledTiles, prevFilledTiles, sourceCell, cells fields.
Related Classes: Coordinate, Direction, Cell, FillableCell, Pipe, TerminationCell
Input: distance : int - the maximum distance (number of steps) water should flow from the source (positive integer).
Output: void
Pre-condition: distance >= 0
Post-condition: Pipes within the specified distance that are connected to the source are marked as filled. filledTiles and prevFilledTiles are updated.

Map::hasLost
Summary: Checks the loss condition: returns true if no new pipes were filled in the previous round.
Algorithm: Return (prevFilledTiles == 0).
Related Features: prevFilledTiles field.
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no new tiles were filled in the previous round, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the loss status based on prevFilledTiles.

Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the specified internal coordinates. Validates coordinates, cell type, and occupancy.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if row is in [1, rows-2] and col is in [1, cols-2]. If not, return false.
  2. Get the cell at cells[row][col].
  3. If the cell is not a FillableCell, return false.
  4. If the cell already has a pipe (pipe field not null), return false.
  5. Set the cell's pipe to the given pipe and return true.
Related Features: cells, rows, cols fields.
Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe
Input: row : int - internal row index (1 to rows-2). col : int - internal column index (1 to cols-2). pipe : Pipe - the pipe to place.
Output: boolean - true if the pipe was successfully placed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: pipe is not null.
Post-condition: If successful, the specified cell's pipe is set to the given pipe. Otherwise, nothing changes.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::hasWon
Summary: Checks if the player has won the game. Win occurs when a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK.
Algorithm: Return map.checkPath().
Related Features: map field.
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if a valid path exists from SOURCE to SINK, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the result of map.checkPath().

Game::hasLost
Summary: Checks if the player has lost the game. Loss occurs when no new tiles were filled in the previous round and the delay has ended.
Algorithm: If delayBar.distance() > 0 and map.hasLost() returns true, then return true; otherwise return false.
Related Features: delayBar, map fields.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the player has lost, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the loss status based on delay and map state.

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Skips the current pipe in the queue without placing it, consuming it and incrementing step count.
Algorithm: Call pipeQueue.consume() and increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: pipeQueue, numOfSteps fields.
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The current pipe is consumed from the queue and numOfSteps is incremented by 1.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Reverts the most recent pipe placement. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. Call cellStack.pop().
  2. If null, return false.
  3. Otherwise, get the coordinate from the popped cell, call map.undo(coord), call pipeQueue.undo(poppedCell.pipe), increment numOfSteps by 1, and return true.
Related Features: cellStack, map, pipeQueue, numOfSteps fields.
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if undo was successful, false if no steps to undo.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If undo was successful, the last placed pipe is removed from the map, returned to the queue, and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Attempts to place the current pipe from the queue onto the map at the specified player-facing coordinates.
Algorithm: 
  1. Convert column letter to internal column index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1.
  2. Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipeQueue.peek()).
  3. If successful, consume the pipe from queue, push the cell onto cellStack, and increment numOfSteps by 1.
  4. Return the success status.
Related Features: map, pipeQueue, cellStack, numOfSteps fields.
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe
Input: row : int - player-facing row number (1-based, maps directly to internal row index). col : char - player-facing column letter ('A', 'B', ...).
Output: boolean - true if the pipe was successfully placed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: row is within [1, map.rows-2], col is within ['A', 'A'+map.cols-3].
Post-condition: If placement was successful, the pipe is placed on the map, consumed from the queue, the cell is pushed onto the stack, and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state by one round: counts down the delay, then fills water tiles according to the current distance.
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown().
  2. If delayBar.distance() > 0, call map.fillTiles(delayBar.distance()).
Related Features: delayBar, map fields.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The delay bar is decremented, and if the delay has ended, water flow is updated.

```text
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::hasWon
Summary: Checks if the player has won the game. Win occurs when a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK.
Algorithm: Return map.checkPath().
Related Features: map field.
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if a valid path exists from SOURCE to SINK, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the result of map.checkPath().

Game::hasLost
Summary: Checks if the player has lost the game. Loss occurs when no new tiles were filled in the previous round and the delay has ended.
Algorithm: If delayBar.distance() > 0 and map.hasLost() returns true, then return true; otherwise return false.
Related Features: delayBar, map fields.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the player has lost, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the loss status based on delay and map state.

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Skips the current pipe in the queue without placing it, consuming it and incrementing step count.
Algorithm: Call pipeQueue.consume() and increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: pipeQueue, numOfSteps fields.
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The current pipe is consumed from the queue and numOfSteps is incremented by 1.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Reverts the most recent pipe placement. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. Call cellStack.pop().
  2. If null, return false.
  3. Otherwise, get the coordinate from the popped cell, call map.undo(coord), call pipeQueue.undo(poppedCell.pipe), increment numOfSteps by 1, and return true.
Related Features: cellStack, map, pipeQueue, numOfSteps fields.
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if undo was successful, false if no steps to undo.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If undo was successful, the last placed pipe is removed from the map, returned to the queue, and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Attempts to place the current pipe from the queue onto the map at the specified player-facing coordinates.
Algorithm: 
  1. Convert column letter to internal column index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1.
  2. Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipeQueue.peek()).
  3. If successful, consume the pipe from queue, push the cell onto cellStack, and increment numOfSteps by 1.
  4. Return the success status.
Related Features: map, pipeQueue, cellStack, numOfSteps fields.
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe
Input: row : int - player-facing row number (1-based, maps directly to internal row index). col : char - player-facing column letter ('A', 'B', ...).
Output: boolean - true if the pipe was successfully placed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: row is within [1, map.rows-2], col is within ['A', 'A'+map.cols-3].
Post-condition: If placement was successful, the pipe is placed on the map, consumed from the queue, the cell is pushed onto the stack, and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state by one round: counts down the delay, then fills water tiles according to the current distance.
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown().
  2. If delayBar.distance() > 0, call map.fillTiles(delayBar.distance()).
Related Features: delayBar, map fields.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The delay bar is decremented, and if the delay has ended, water flow is updated.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the

  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
```

Summary: Reverts the most recent pipe placement. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. Call cellStack.pop().
  2. If null, return false.
  3. Otherwise, get the coordinate from the popped cell, call map.undo(coord), call pipeQueue.undo(poppedCell.pipe), increment numOfSteps by 1, and return true.

Summary: Attempts to place the current pipe from the queue onto the map at the specified player-facing coordinates.
Algorithm: 
  1. Convert column letter to internal column index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1.
  2. Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipeQueue.peek()).
  3. If successful, consume the pipe from queue, push the cell onto cellStack, and increment numOfSteps by 1.
  4. Return the success status.
Related Features: map, pipeQueue, cellStack, numOfSteps fields.
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe
Input: row : int - player-facing row number (1-based, maps directly to internal row index). col : char - player-facing column letter ('A', 'B', ...).
Output: boolean - true if the pipe was successfully placed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: row is within [1, map.rows-2], col is within ['A', 'A'+map.cols-3].
Post-condition: If placement was successful, the pipe is placed on the map, consumed from the queue, the cell is pushed onto the stack, and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state by one round: counts down the delay, then fills water tiles according to the current distance.
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown().
  2. If delayBar.distance() == 0, call map.fillBeginTile() to mark the source as filled.
  3. If delayBar.distance() > 0, call map.fillTiles(delayBar.distance()).
Related Features: delayBar, map fields.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The delay bar is decremented, the source tile is filled when delay ends, and water flow is updated according to the current distance.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::hasWon
Summary: Checks if the player has won the game. Win occurs when a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK.
Algorithm: Return map.checkPath().
Related Features: map field.
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if a valid path exists from SOURCE to SINK, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the result of map.checkPath().

Game::hasLost
Summary: Checks if the player has lost the game. Loss occurs when no new tiles were filled in the previous round and the delay has ended.
Algorithm: If delayBar.distance() > 0 and map.hasLost() returns true, then return true; otherwise return false.
Related Features: delayBar, map fields.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the player has lost, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the loss status based on delay and map state.

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Skips the current pipe in the queue without placing it, consuming it and incrementing step count.
Algorithm: Call pipeQueue.consume() and increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: pipeQueue, numOfSteps fields.
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The current pipe is consumed from the queue and numOfSteps is incremented by 1.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Reverts the most recent pipe placement. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. Call cellStack.pop().
  2. If null, return false.
  3. Otherwise, get the coordinate from the popped cell, call map.undo(coord), call pipeQueue.undo(poppedCell.pipe), increment numOfSteps by 1, and return true.
Related Features: cellStack, map, pipeQueue, numOfSteps fields.
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if undo was successful, false if no steps to undo.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If undo was successful, the last placed pipe is removed from the map, returned to the queue, and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Attempts to place the current pipe from the queue onto the map at the specified player-facing coordinates.
Algorithm: 
  1. Convert column letter to internal column index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1.
  2. Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipeQueue.peek()).
  3. If successful, consume the pipe from queue, push the cell onto cellStack, and increment numOfSteps by 1.
  4. Return the success status.
Related Features: map, pipeQueue, cellStack, numOfSteps fields.
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe
Input: row : int - player-facing row number (1-based, maps directly to internal row index). col : char - player-facing column letter ('A', 'B', ...).
Output: boolean - true if the pipe was successfully placed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: row is within [1, map.rows-2], col is within ['A', 'A'+map.cols-3].
Post-condition: If placement was successful, the pipe is placed on the map, consumed from the queue, the cell is pushed onto the stack, and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state by one round: counts down the delay, then fills water tiles according to the current distance.
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown().
  2. If delayBar.distance() == 0, call map.fillBeginTile() to mark the source as filled.
  3. If delayBar.distance() > 0, call map.fillTiles(delayBar.distance()).
Related Features: delayBar, map fields.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The delay bar is decremented, the source tile is filled when delay ends, and water flow is updated according to the current distance.

```text
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation.
```

# Operation Specifications
PipeQueue::consume
Summary: Removes and discards the head pipe from the queue, then auto-refills the queue to maintain its fixed length.
Algorithm:
  1. Remove the first element from pipeQueue.
  2. Call generateNewPipe() and add the result to the end of pipeQueue.
Related Features: pipeQueue field.
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: pipeQueue is not empty.
Post-condition: The head pipe is removed, and a new random pipe is appended to maintain the queue length.

PipeQueue::undo
Summary: Inserts a pipe back to the front of the queue.
Algorithm: Add the given pipe to the beginning (index 0) of pipeQueue.
Related Features: pipeQueue field.
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: pipe : Pipe - the pipe to be returned to the front of the queue.
Output: void
Pre-condition: pipe is not null.
Post-condition: The given pipe is inserted at the front of the queue.

PipeQueue::generateNewPipe
Summary: Creates a new pipe with a random shape.
Algorithm: Generate a random PipeShape (one of the seven shapes) and return new Pipe with that shape and filled=false.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: Pipe, PipeShape
Input: None
Output: Pipe - a new unfilled pipe with a random shape.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns a new Pipe object with a randomly selected shape.

PipeQueue::peek
Summary: Returns the head pipe of the queue without removing it.
Algorithm: Return the first element of pipeQueue.
Related Features: pipeQueue field.
Related Classes: Pipe
Input: None
Output: Pipe - the current head pipe of the queue.
Pre-condition: pipeQueue is not empty.
Post-condition: Returns the first element of the queue without modifying it.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short

  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
```

public void fillTiles(final int distance) {
    if (distance == 1) {
        fillBeginTile();
    }
    
    int newFilledTiles = 0;
    
    // Get source cell
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    if (source == null) {
        prevFilledTiles = 0;
        return;
    }
    
    Direction pointingTo = source.getPointingTo();
    Coordinate sourceCoord = source.getCoord();
    
    // Compute starting cell (adjacent to source in pointingTo direction)
    int startRow = sourceCoord.getRow();
    int startCol = sourceCoord.getCol();
    switch (pointingTo.getValue()) {
        case Direction.UP_VALUE:
            startRow--;
            break;
        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
            startRow++;
            break;
        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
            startCol--;
            break;
        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
            startCol++;
            break;
    }
    
    // BFS
    boolean[][] visited = new boolean[rows][cols];
    Queue<int[]> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    
    // Check starting cell
    if (startRow >= 0 && startRow < rows && startCol >= 0 && startCol < cols) {
        queue.add(new int[]{startRow, startCol, 1});
        visited[startRow][startCol] = true;
    }
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        int[] current = queue.poll();
        int r = current[0];
        int c = current[1];
        int depth = current[2];
        
        Cell cell = getCell()[r][c];
        if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
            continue;
        }
        FillableCell fc = (FillableCell) cell;
        Pipe pipe = fc.getPipe();
        if (pipe == null) {
            continue;
        }
        
        // Mark as filled
        if (!pipe.isFilled()) {
            pipe.setFilled(true);
            newFilledTiles++;
            getFilledTiles().add(fc.getCoord());
        }
        
        if (depth >= distance) {
            continue;
        }
        
        // Check each connection direction
        for (Direction dir : pipe.getConnections()) {
            int nr = r;
            int nc = c;
            switch (dir.getValue()) {
                case Direction.UP_VALUE:
                    nr--;
                    break;
                case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
                    nr++;
                    break;
                case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
                    nc--;
                    break;
                case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
                    nc++;
                    break;
            }
            
            // Check bounds
            if (nr < 0 || nr >= rows || nc < 0 || nc >= cols) {
                continue;
            }
            if (visited[nr][nc]) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
            if (!(neighborCell instanceof FillableCell)) {
                continue;
            }
            FillableCell neighborFc = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFc.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe == null) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Check if neighbor's pipe has connection in opposite direction
            Direction opposite = getOpposite(dir);
            if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                visited[nr][nc] = true;
                queue.add(new int[]{nr, nc, depth + 1});
            }
        }
    }
    
    prevFilledTiles = newFilledTiles;
}
private Direction getOpposite(Direction dir) {
    switch (dir.getValue()) {
        case Direction.UP_VALUE: return Direction.DOWN;
        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: return Direction.UP;
        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: return Direction.RIGHT;
        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: return Direction.LEFT;
    }
    return null;
}

public boolean tryPlacePipe(final int row, final int col, final Pipe pipe) {
    if (row < 1 || row > getRows() - 2 || col < 1 || col > getCols() - 2) {

public void fillTiles(final int distance) {
    if (distance == 1) {
        fillBeginTile();
    }
    
    // Get source cell and its pointing direction
    TerminationCell source = getSourceCell();
    Direction dir = source.getPointingTo();
    
    // Get the offset for the direction
    Coordinate offset = getOffsetForDirection(dir);
    
    // Starting cell is adjacent to source in the pointingTo direction
    Coordinate startCoord = source.getCoord().add(offset);
    
    // BFS
    java.util.Queue<Coordinate> queue = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
    java.util.Map<Coordinate, Integer> depthMap = new java.util.HashMap<>();
    java.util.Set<Coordinate> visited = new java.util.HashSet<>();
    
    queue.add(startCoord);
    visited.add(startCoord);
    depthMap.put(startCoord, 1);
    
    int newFilledCount = 0;
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int currentDepth = depthMap.get(current);
        
        if (currentDepth > distance) {
            continue;
        }
        
        Cell currentCell = getCell()[current.getRow()][current.getCol()];
        if (!(currentCell instanceof FillableCell)) {
            continue;
        }
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) currentCell;
        Pipe pipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
        if (pipe == null) {
            continue;
        }
        
        // Mark this cell as filled
        if (!pipe.isFilled()) {
            pipe.setFilled(true);
            getFilledTiles().add(current);
            newFilledCount++;
        }
        
        // Explore connections
        for (Direction connDir : pipe.getConnections()) {
            Coordinate neighborOffset = getOffsetForDirection(connDir);
            Coordinate neighborCoord = current.add(neighborOffset);
            
            if (visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
                continue;
            }
            
            int neighborRow = neighborCoord.getRow();
            int neighborCol = neighborCoord.getCol();
            
            if (neighborRow < 0 || neighborRow >= getRows() || neighborCol < 0 || neighborCol >= getCols()) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Cell neighborCell = getCell()[neighborRow][neighborCol];
            if (!(neighborCell instanceof FillableCell)) {
                continue;
            }
            FillableCell neighborFillable = (FillableCell) neighborCell;
            Pipe neighborPipe = neighborFillable.getPipe();
            if (neighborPipe == null) {
                continue;
            }
            
            // Check if neighbor's pipe has connection in opposite direction
            Direction opposite = getOppositeDirection(connDir);
            if (neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(opposite)) {
                visited.add(neighborCoord);
                depthMap.put(neighborCoord, currentDepth + 1);
                queue.add(neighborCoord);
            }
        }
    }
    
    setPrevFilledTiles(newFilledCount);
}

public boolean hasLost() {
    return getPrevFilledTiles() == 0;
}

private Coordinate getOffset(Direction dir) {
    Coordinate offset = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
    switch (dir.getValue()) {
        case Direction.UP_VALUE:
            offset.setRow(-1);
            offset.setCol(0);
            break;
        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE:
            offset.setRow(1);
            offset.setCol(0);
            break;
        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE:
            offset.setRow(0);
            offset.setCol(-1);
            break;
        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE:
            offset.setRow(0);
            offset.setCol(1);
            break;
    }
    return offset;
}
private Direction getOpposite(Direction dir) {
    switch (dir.getValue()) {
        case Direction.UP_VALUE: return Direction.DOWN;
        case Direction.DOWN_VALUE: return Direction.UP;
        case Direction.LEFT_VALUE: return Direction.RIGHT;
        case Direction.RIGHT_VALUE: return Direction.LEFT;
    }
    return null;
}
